sample_unit: LLM responses to scenarios (5 LLMs x scenarios, initial diagnosis)

links.outcome: Recognition of urgent upper extremity emergencies (e.g., compartment syndrome) across initial and ongoing inquiry
links.effect: Compartment syndrome misidentified as nonurgent in 80% of scenarios on initial inquiry; four of five LLMs corrected on continued inquiry. Repeat at 24 months: 100% PPV, 95% NPV initially, 98% NPV after ongoing inquiry.
links.quote: Compartment syndrome was misidentified as nonurgent in 80% of scenarios on initial inquiry, although four of five LLMs corrected on continued inquiry.

links.outcome: Missed and unnecessary escalation of urgent versus nonurgent symptom scenarios
links.effect: Nonurgent discernment 97% PPV and 89% NPV on initial query, improving to 96% and 97% after ongoing inquiry; compartment syndrome missed in 80% initially.
links.quote: LLMs discerned nonurgent conditions with 97% positive predictive value (PPV) and an 89% negative predictive value (NPV) on initial query, which improved to 96% and 97% respectively after ongoing inquiry.

links.outcome: Clinical and safety performance for prompts written below a sixth grade reading level
links.effect: With sixth-grade-level scenarios, urgency NPV 89% initially (97% after ongoing inquiry); diagnosis correct or partially correct for 115 of 150 (82%).
links.quote: Diagnosis was correct or partially correct for 115 of 150 (82%) on initial inquiry.

unlisted_practices: Re-running the LLM assessment after 24 months with current model versions to detect performance change
Iterative follow-up questioning (asking the LLM what additional information it needs) to improve triage accuracy

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial LLM chatbots on their ability to triage simulated urgent vs nonurgent upper extremity symptom vignettes without testing an organizational deployment safeguard or guardrail.
